# Evaluating ∫ -x³ · exp(x) dx

## Method: Tabular Integration by Parts

I'll first compute ∫ x³ · exp(x) dx using the tabular method, then apply the negative sign.

| Sign | Differentiate | Integrate |
|:----:|:-------------:|:---------:|
| + | x³ | exp(x) |
| − | 3x² | x·exp(x) |
| + | 6x | x²·exp(x) |
| − | 6 | x³·exp(x) |
| + | 0 | x⁴·exp(x) |

Reading along the diagonals:

$$\int x^3 e^x \, dx = x^3 e^x - 3x^2 e^x + 6x e^x - 6e^x + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
- d/dx[x³·exp(x)] = 3x²·exp(x) + x³·exp(x)
- d/dx[-3x²·exp(x)] = -6x·exp(x) - 3x²·exp(x)
- d/dx[6x·exp(x)] = 6·exp(x) + 6x·exp(x)
- d/dx[-6·exp(x)] = -6·exp(x)

Sum: x³·exp(x) ✓

## Applying the Negative Sign

$$\int -x^3 e^x \, dx = -x^3 e^x + 3x^2 e^x - 6x e^x + 6e^x + C$$

## Quick Check

Differentiating: (-3x² - x³)·exp(x) + (6x + 3x²)·exp(x) + (-6 - 6x)·exp(x) + 6·exp(x) = -x³·exp(x) ✓

<answer>-x**3*exp(x) + 3*x**2*exp(x) - 6*x*exp(x) + 6*exp(x) + C</answer>
